Our project investigates how psychological symptoms relate to one another over time and whether group-level symptom relationships adequately describe the dynamics of an individual. We use simulated daily symptom
ratings, Bayesian VAR models, and an interactive Shiny app to explore individual differences in temporal symptom networks.

## 5. Explore the Shiny app

The project includes an initial Shiny app designed to make the comparison between group-level and participant-level temporal symptom networks interactive.

Users can generate simulated participant data or upload a CSV containing daily ratings for the six symptoms: down, tired, sleep, nervous, worry, and irritable. The app displays the participant's estimated temporal network alongside the group network and provides a table comparing edge estimates and their differences. Users can also adjust the network display settings.

The app uses a Bayesian lag-one VAR model to estimate temporal associations between symptoms. These associations describe predictive relationships across consecutive days and should not be interpreted as proof of causation. Simulated participant data are illustrative and do not represent observed clinical responses.
